claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
Controlled post-synthesis aging can induce nanoscale precipitates in the TiVNbTa BCC matrix.
The aging-induced precipitates will be thermally stable at elevated temperature.
An intermediate-temperature aging hold for a defined duration will promote in-situ precipitation of fine secondary phases.
The precipitates may form at grain boundaries or be distributed uniformly within the BCC matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates will pin dislocations.
The nanoscale precipitates will inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
The precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion and impede elevated-temperature slip.
The precipitates will retard high-temperature creep deformation.
Obstructing dislocation motion and elevated-temperature slip will increase the alloy's yield strength.
The baseline as-cast TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Aging-induced precipitation is predicted to increase yield strength at 1273 K by approximately 20–30% relative to the 330 MPa baseline.
The precipitate-strengthened alloy is predicted to retain adequate ductility for use as an intermediate heat-transfer layer.
The intervention is expected to remain effective at operating temperatures up to approximately 1273 K.
Precipitate coarsening during long-term service could compromise the intended strengthening effect.
The strength improvement and ductility trade-off depend on precipitation kinetics, precipitate size and distribution, and long-term thermal stability under cyclic loading.
The proposed comparison will test aged and untreated TiVNbTa samples at 1273 K under comparable strain rates.
TEM and XRD will be used to determine whether nanoscale precipitates form and remain stable.
